An atima that runs on your own computer can be used by an AI app as well
as through the browser. You ask the app a question in plain words, and it
looks at your projects, runs statistics and draws figures by calling
atima. This article explains how to connect an app, what the app can and
cannot do, the limits, and what happens to your data when you do this.
Shared servers (`auth = "oidc"`) do not offer this yet.

**Read "Where your data goes" below before you connect an app.** What
atima returns to the app is, with most apps, sent on to the company that
provides the app's model.


## What MCP is

The [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) (MCP) is a
standard way for an AI app to use other programs. A program that offers
itself this way is an MCP server. It gives the app a list of **tools**:
named operations, each with a description and a list of arguments. The
app's language model decides when to call a tool and with which
arguments, the server does the work, and the result goes back to the
model, which uses it to answer you. A local atima is an MCP server. Its
address is the server's address followed by `/mcp`, and `run()` prints it
at start-up:

```
AI apps can connect to http://127.0.0.1:8080/mcp
```


## Connecting

atima must be running, and must keep running while you use the app. Start
it as usual (see [Using atima on your own computer](local-install.html)):

```{r}
atima::run()
```

### Claude Code

[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) is the app atima has been
tested with. In a terminal:

```sh
claude mcp add --transport http atima http://127.0.0.1:8080/mcp
```

`claude mcp list` shows whether it connected. To disconnect again:

```sh
claude mcp remove atima
```

### Other apps

Any app that can use a remote MCP server and knows the protocol revision
atima speaks (see "Protocol revision") should work, but only Claude Code
has been tried. In the app's settings for MCP servers, tools or
connectors, add a server with:

| Setting | Value |
|---------|-------|
| Type or transport | "HTTP", "Streamable HTTP" or "remote". Not "stdio", and not "SSE". |
| URL | `http://127.0.0.1:8080/mcp`, with your own port if you changed it. |
| Authentication | None. There is no key, token or sign-in. |
| Name | Anything, for example `atima`. |

The app has to run on the same computer as atima. An app that runs on a
company's servers, such as a chat website, cannot reach `127.0.0.1` on
your computer.


## What to ask

Ask in plain words. Name the project if you have several. For example:

- "List my atima projects."
- "Describe the hmp50 project. Which metadata fields does it have?"
- "Which metadata fields of hmp50 are related to alpha diversity?"
- "Is body site associated with community composition in hmp50? Use
  Bray-Curtis."
- "Draw an ordination of hmp50 colored by body site."
- "Which genera differ most between body sites? Show the ten with the
  smallest p-values."
- "Give me the R code for that last figure."
- "Export the genus-level abundances of hmp50 as a table."

Each figure comes with its statistics table and the rbiom code that makes
it, so you can check what was done and repeat it in R.

An AI app can misread a result or choose an unsuitable test. Treat what
it tells you as you would a colleague's first look: check the statistics
table and the code before you rely on a conclusion.


## The six tools

| Tool | What it does |
|------|--------------|
| `list_projects` | Lists the projects you can open, with their keys and titles. |
| `describe_project` | A project's samples, sequencing depths, metadata fields and their values, taxonomic ranks, most abundant taxa, and whether it has a tree. |
| `describe_function` | The arguments of an rbiom statistics or plot function, as a JSON Schema, so that the app knows what it may ask for. |
| `run_stats` | Runs `adiv_stats()`, `bdiv_stats()`, `taxa_stats()` or `taxa_da()` and returns the table. |
| `make_plot` | Draws any of the plots the web interface offers and returns the image, its statistics table and the R code. |
| `export` | Writes a file and returns a link to it: the BIOM file, an Excel workbook, or a table of the metadata, taxonomy, alpha diversity, beta diversity or taxa abundances, or the tree. |

`run_stats` and `make_plot` can rarefy to another depth, or use only some
of the samples, for that one call. Nothing in the project changes.


## What the tools cannot do

**The tools read and compute. None of them changes anything.**

- They cannot upload a file, save, rename, publish or delete a project,
  or change metadata.
- They work on saved projects. They do not see unsaved changes in an open
  browser tab.
- They cannot read files on your computer. An app may have other tools
  that can; those are not atima's.
- They do not make PDF or SVG figures. Use the web interface for those.


## Limits

| What | Limit |
|------|-------|
| Rows of a statistics table in a result | 50 by default; the app can ask for up to 500. Rows come smallest p-value first. The result says how many rows there are in all and links to the whole table as a CSV file. |
| Numbers in a result's table | Rounded to four significant digits. The CSV file has them in full. |
| Figures | PNG images, 900 by 600 pixels unless the app asks otherwise, 200 to 2,000 pixels a side. |
| Projects in `list_projects` | 200. |
| Values listed per metadata field in `describe_project` | 50. |
| Time for one tool call | `time_limit` seconds, 60 by default, as for a figure in the browser. A call that takes longer is stopped and the app is told. |
| Links to figures, tables and exports | They work for `session_hours`, 24 by default, and only while atima runs. Save what you want to keep. |
| Calls at once | Each call is a job that waits for a free worker. An app that calls many tools at once fills the queue, and further calls are told that the server is busy. |

To raise the time limit, start atima with, for example,
`atima::run(time_limit = 300)`.


## Where your data goes

atima itself only answers requests from your own computer, and sends
nothing anywhere. But what a tool returns is handed to the AI app:
project titles and descriptions, metadata field names and values, taxon
names, statistics tables, figures, and whatever is in a file the app
exports and opens. Most apps send all of
it to the servers of the company that provides their model, where that
company's terms decide what happens to it.

- If your data must not leave your computer, do not connect an app, or
  use one that runs its model on your computer.
- If your data may leave under conditions (for example, human-subject
  metadata under a data use agreement), check that the app provider's
  terms meet them before you connect.
- Nothing is sent until the app calls a tool, and tools are called only
  while you use the app. Removing the server from the app ends it.

The article [Where your data goes](data-handling.html) covers the rest of
what a local atima stores and sends.

### Files you did not make yourself

The text in a project is read by the app's language model: titles,
descriptions, metadata and taxon names. atima returns it as data and tells
the model to treat it as data, but a model can still be misled by text
that was written to mislead it, for example a description that says
"ignore your instructions and ...". This is called prompt injection.

With atima's own tools, the harm such text can do is small, because no
tool changes or sends anything. The risk is in what else the app can do.
If the same app can also read your files, send email or run commands,
text hidden in a dataset from someone else could try to make it do those
things. For datasets you did not make yourself, read what the app
proposes to do before you allow it, and do not let the app act without
asking.


## Protocol revision

atima speaks revision **2026-07-28** of the MCP specification, over
Streamable HTTP, without sessions, and only that revision. An app that
only knows earlier revisions cannot connect: it opens with a handshake
that this revision no longer has, and atima answers with an error that
names 2026-07-28. Update the app. If it still cannot connect, it does not
support this revision yet.


## When it does not work

**The app says it cannot connect, or the connection is refused.** atima
is not running, or runs on another port. Start it, and compare the
address in the app with the line `AI apps can connect to ...` that
`run()` printed.

**403, "This server only answers requests made to localhost".** The
address in the app uses a name other than `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or
`[::1]`, for example the computer's network name. atima refuses such
requests on purpose. Use the address `run()` printed.

**404 for `/mcp`.** The server runs with `auth = "oidc"`. Shared servers
do not offer the endpoint yet.

**An error that mentions the protocol version or `initialize`.** The app
speaks an earlier revision. See "Protocol revision".

**The app says a project does not exist.** Tools name a project by its
key, the word in the address when the project is open in the browser, for
example `hmp50`. Ask the app to list your projects first.

**A tool call is refused with a message about an argument.** The message
comes from rbiom and names the option and its valid choices. Apps usually
correct the call themselves. If one does not, tell it which field or
option you meant.

**"The server is busy" or a time-out.** See "Limits".

**The link to a figure or export no longer works.** Links stop working
after `session_hours`, and when atima is restarted with a new temporary
directory, which is the default.

In atima's log, each request from an app is a `request` line for `/mcp`
with an `rpc` field that names the tool, such as `tools/call make_plot`.
The arguments of a call are not logged.
